scenario.title: Support backlog
scenario.initial_request: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

CL-01.statement: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

CL-02.statement: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.

H-REQUESTER-FRAMING.statement: Customers experience high waiting times for refund answers, motivating a chatbot to reduce wait.

H-POLICY-CONFUSION.statement: Unclear or frequently changing refund policies generate many customer inquiries, causing ticket backlog.

H-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: Insufficient support staff or inadequate training leads to slow responses and ticket accumulation.

H-SYSTEM-LATENCY.statement: Slow retrieval of refund status from payment-db causes agents to keep tickets open while waiting for data.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Median response time is 2 hours, well below the 24‑hour SLA, indicating customers are not experiencing high waiting times despite 900 tickets.
The observation shows five refund records failing due to IBAN format errors, indicating a technical issue that can generate customer inquiries about refunds.

E-03.content: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder perceives that customers experience high waiting times for refund answers and believes a chatbot would provide instant responses, indicating a perceived need to reduce wait.

U-U1.question: What proportion of tickets are attributable to IBAN format failures?
U-U1.resolution_path: Tag tickets with refund failure reason and analyse correlation.
U-U1.safe_placeholder: Assume 10 % of tickets are IBAN‑related for capacity planning.

U-U2.question: How effective is reducing IBAN failures at lowering perceived waiting time?
U-U2.resolution_path: Run a controlled experiment measuring ticket volume and customer satisfaction before/after IBAN‑validation fix.
U-U2.safe_placeholder: Deploy IBAN‑validation improvement and monitor median response time and ticket count.

A-A1.statement: Each IBAN format failure generates at least one customer inquiry ticket.

A-A2.statement: Increased ticket volume leads to perceived high waiting times despite low median response time.

SC-SC1.statement: Maintain median response time under 1 hour.

SC-SC2.statement: Eliminate IBAN format failures in refund payments.

SC-SC3.statement: Reduce refund‑related ticket volume by 30 % relative to baseline.
SC-SC3.validation_method: Compare ticket-db ticket count for refund‑related tags before/after intervention

details.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

structural_remedies.description: Add IBAN format validation before processing refund payments in payment-db and enforce correct IBAN entry in the payment UI.
structural_remedies.rationale: Can be implemented as a configuration or validation rule change; no new development required.; residual gap: Other sources of refund-related tickets (e.g., policy confusion) may persist, so perceived waiting time may not drop to zero.

framing_assertion.rationale: The requester frames the problem as customers waiting too long for refund answers, implying high waiting time.

hypotheses.statement: Customers experience high waiting times for refund answers, motivating a chatbot to reduce wait.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, a chatbot directly addresses the stated problem and would likely reduce ticket volume.

hypotheses.statement: Unclear or frequently changing refund policies generate many customer inquiries, causing ticket backlog.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, improving policy communication or self‑service FAQs would reduce tickets more than a chatbot alone.

hypotheses.statement: Insufficient support staff or inadequate training leads to slow responses and ticket accumulation.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, increasing headcount or better training would cut wait times; a chatbot would only deflect some queries.

hypotheses.statement: Slow retrieval of refund status from payment-db causes agents to keep tickets open while waiting for data.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, optimizing the payment-db query or caching would shorten handling time; a chatbot would not fix the underlying latency.

actions.question: What are the current response times for refund-related tickets?
actions.decision_impact_rationale: High response times would support building a chatbot; low times would weaken the case.
actions.why_now: Provides direct evidence on waiting time and system latency, key to evaluating the requester's framing and latency hypothesis.

actions.question: What is the frequency and pattern of refund failures in the payment database?
actions.decision_impact_rationale: High failure rates could indicate policy confusion driving repeat contacts; low rates would suggest other causes.
actions.why_now: Helps test whether policy confusion is generating refund-related tickets that contribute to backlog.

actions.question: Interview the support lead to uncover perceived causes of refund ticket backlog and any biases in the request.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: Direct insight from the stakeholder can confirm or refute multiple hypotheses and reveal framing bias.
actions.why_now: A single interview can discriminate among all competing hypotheses and clarify the stakeholder's potential bias.
